i can be extremely bullish on a chart one week and completely bearish the next if price action invalidates my original thesis

all-time high breakouts are a good example. they used to be some of the easiest trades in crypto, especially back in 2017

now failed breakouts can lead to aggressive sell-offs as everyone rushes to exit the same trade

i think a lot of traders struggle with accepting that the market has changed direction, and by the time they do, a significant part of the move has already happened

the way crypto trades around all-time highs has changed significantly since 2017

back then, buying new highs was one of my most reliable setups. by 2021, i started getting punished for trading those breakouts the same way

markets began consolidating around previous highs, breaking out briefly, then reversing aggressively

i've had to adapt by paying much closer attention to failed breakouts and how price reacts when it retests key levels

with equities also showing signs of weakness, i'm watching the NASDAQ and S&P 500 closely

a normal 10% correction in stocks could still create significant downside pressure for crypto

time is an underrated part of risk management when trading lower timeframes

when i enter a trade expecting a sharp move, i want price to react relatively quickly

if Bitcoin is sitting around my entry for too long without moving in the direction i expected, i start questioning the setup

the advantage of trading lower timeframes is that you can recognize when something isn't working much earlier

sometimes i'll exit a trade simply because it's taking too long to play out, even if my stop hasn't been hit

price and time both matter when deciding whether a trade is still worth taking

i've been thinking about the possibility that crypto topped before equities this cycle

if the recent bounce is just a countertrend move and stocks are only now beginning a larger correction, crypto could still have another leg lower

i'm not fully convinced that's the scenario we're heading into, but i think it's worth considering given how much AI and equities have driven risk appetite this cycle

Bitcoin could also find its bottom before the broader equity market does, even if both continue selling off in the near term

i'm keeping an open mind and watching how price reacts as these markets approach important levels

$ZEC is an extremely misunderstood asset, which is why there's still so much upside left.

ZEC started to bottom around April 2025, when @ebfull shared a blog post about Project Tachyon. Tachyon makes Zcash quantum proof and paves the way to scale Zcash to 50k TPS. And you cannot address quantum without addressing scalability since post-quantum cryptographic signatures are going to be an order of magnitude larger.

At the risk of sounding hyperbolic, the real bull case for Zcash is to fulfill Satoshi's vision: becoming peer-to-peer electronic digital cash. What many Bitcoiners gave up on. Zcash has the same properties as BTC, except it has a credible roadmap to scale to 50k TPS at the base layer, with built-in privacy. It's extremely ambitious, but that is the vision.

At the same time, I expect Bitcoin to undergo a crisis of confidence. Crypto participants have been conditioned to blindly believe BTC will hit new highs every couple of years. I believe these assumptions will be challenged as the quantum overhang looms large, and continued underperformance will drive more flows into ZEC. I would not be surprised if BTC trades like ETH last cycle.

Peter Thiel talks about the "Last Mover Advantage." That is, it's far better to make the last great development in a market and then dominate. Facebook vs Myspace. Google vs Yahoo. Zcash has dominated a small niche (privacy), and then it plans to scale to the ambitious goal, which is peer-to-peer electronic cash.

The ZEC trade closely resembles the SOL trade last cycle. ZEC's ability to move fast challenges a slow-moving incumbent (BTC), similar to how SOL challenged the ivory tower of ETH. History doesn't repeat, but it often rhymes.

There’s a fundamental mismatch between why Zcash is going up (Tachyon + last mover advantage) and the broader market’s understanding ("just a privacy coin"). Understanding this is a form of alpha/edge. I expect this knowledge gap to close when Tachyon hits mainnet in Q1 2027.

As a result, I expect the following over the next 1-2yrs:
1) Bitcoiners will start "silent quitting" and begin hedging their holdings with ZEC
2) Capital allocators that may have full ported BTC 5 years ago, will buy both ZEC and BTC as a bet on a sovereign SoV
